questions.question: Source A. Lumora makes rice cookers in Singapore. For three years its home sales have been flat at 400,000 a year at $50 each, and two low-priced importers now share the same supermarket shelves. Its fixed costs are $4.8m a year and each cooker costs $26 in materials, labour and energy. The directors plan to export 200,000 cookers a year to Belmar, where household disposable income is $4,000 and rising 7% a year, three supermarket chains sell most small appliances, and foreign firms may own no more than 49% of a distribution business. They are also choosing a site for a new $20m factory expected to earn $3m a year. Inside the trade bloc that includes Belmar, labour would cost $6 a cooker and freight $1. Outside it, labour would cost $4 and freight $2, cookers entering the bloc pay a 10% tariff, and the government offers a $5m grant. Other costs are $10 a cooker at either site. The exchange rate is $1 = 4 units of Belmar's currency, and engineers and technicians are in short supply in Singapore. Explain one push factor that may have led Lumora to plan exports. (4 marks)
